blindSummary:
This country is, on paper, one of the region's legal pioneers on trans rights. A 2016 gender-identity law was ground-breaking: legal gender recognition on the basis of self-declared identity (an administrative process, no surgery), and gender identity is an explicitly protected ground in anti-discrimination law. The constitution also names gender identity.

Implementation lags the statute: the first national LGBTQ+ survey (2024) reveals significant exclusion in health, education, employment, and housing; social conservatism is strong outside the main urban centres; and line officials often resist applying the gender-identity law. There is no documented pattern of police targeting of trans people as such, and no traveler-facing restriction — but also limited effective protection outside major cities.
blindOutOfScope: LGR mechanics and discrimination-law enforcement gaps are resident-facing.
blindSourceSummaries: Academic comparative-politics article (April 2024) on activists, parties and the expansion of trans rights in this country: the country prohibits gender-identity discrimination and passed a ground-breaking gender-identity law (2016, allowing name/marker change) despite low voter support; trans activists leveraged access to ruling-party legislators; contradictory heteronormative laws passed alongside because both organised religion and LGBT activists were party constituents.

NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (WordPress critical error); the underlying LGBTI news-agency article (Dec 2024) covers this country's first virtual survey revealing the great exclusion of LGBTI people.

A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: general human-rights assessment (arbitrary deprivation of life, prison conditions, corruption) - the LGBT section documents the constitutional anti-discrimination guarantee and societal discrimination.

Foreign newsmagazine (July 2017): a foreign state's transgender military ban left that state off a short list of countries that do not legally discriminate on gender identity in the armed forces - comparative context including this country's military policy.

A medical-education and research foundation's page on sexual and reproductive rights in this country: the constitution prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity and guarantees sexual rights; documents the legal framework including abortion law.

National news site (Aug 2014): gay military personnel in this country's armed forces live between discrimination and clandestinity - a soldier's hidden relationship with a senior officer; an LGBT collective and human-rights defenders call for openness in the institution.
blindLocalsOnly: The gender-identity law's administrative process, and its uneven implementation by line officials, are resident-facing; the 2024 survey exclusion data describes residents' lives.
